diagnosis_plain: Uncomplicated Diabetes Mellitus (Insulin-Dependent) — no ketoacidosis, stable at presentation

pet.chief_complaint: 3-week history of polyuria/polydipsia, weight loss ~2 kg despite polyphagia
pet.report_type: Serum biochemistry panel, CBC, urinalysis with sediment
pet.history: No prior chronic illness; weight loss and increased thirst noticed 3–4 weeks ago; appetite remained strong throughout

summary.severity: Significant — chronic uncontrolled hyperglycemia; insulin therapy must begin immediately
summary.decision_window: Start treatment now — uncomplicated DM at ideal window; delay increases DKA and cataract risk
summary.prognosis: Excellent with consistent insulin management; ~80% of dogs achieve stable regulation within 1–3 months
summary.paths: 4 paths: Vetsulin · NPH (human insulin) · Glargine (off-label) · CGM home monitoring (add-on)
summary.priority_match: Vetsulin best fits stable long-term control goal; CGM add-on reduces clinic burden significantly
summary.next_step: Begin Vetsulin 0.25–0.5 U/kg BID with a consistent high-fiber diet; schedule first glucose curve at day 7–10

findings.name: Blood Glucose
findings.meaning: Markedly elevated — confirms uncontrolled hyperglycemia consistent with diabetes mellitus

findings.name: Fructosamine
findings.meaning: Reflects average blood glucose over the past 2–3 weeks — rules out stress hyperglycemia; confirms chronically elevated glucose

findings.name: Urine Glucose / Ketones
findings.meaning: Glucose above renal threshold confirms DM; absence of ketones rules out diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) — critical safety finding

findings.name: ALT (Liver Enzyme)
findings.meaning: Mildly elevated — secondary hepatic lipidosis from DM; expected to normalize with glucose control

findings.name: BUN / Creatinine
findings.meaning: Kidney function intact — no concurrent renal disease; does not restrict insulin dosing

findings.name: CBC — Neutrophils
findings.meaning: Consistent with stress leukogram from chronic illness; no active infection identified requiring separate treatment

paths.label: Option A
paths.survival: Excellent; FDA-approved for canine DM; ~80% achieve stable regulation within 1–3 months; best long-term evidence base
paths.aligns: First-line standard; your vet will know the dosing protocol well; predictable 10–14 hour action curve; consistent BID schedule fits most households
paths.tensions: BID injections required; strict feeding schedule needed; glucose curves every 1–3 months initially; some dogs show variability in response

paths.label: Option B
paths.approach: NPH Insulin (Humulin N) — Off-Label Human Insulin
paths.survival: Good; comparable outcomes to Vetsulin in many dogs; widely used in cost-sensitive situations with appropriate monitoring
paths.aligns: Significantly lower cost; some dogs respond equally or better to NPH; available at any pharmacy without vet order
paths.tensions: Off-label use (not FDA-approved for dogs); slightly shorter action duration (8–12 hrs) may require closer timing; same monitoring intensity as Vetsulin

paths.label: Option C
paths.survival: Variable in dogs; better-suited to cats; some dogs need TID dosing for adequate control; limited canine-specific long-term data
paths.aligns: Flatter action curve reduces peak hypoglycemia risk; useful if hypoglycemic episodes occur on other insulins
paths.tensions: Not standard first-line for dogs; less predictable in canine patients than in cats; insufficient canine outcome data; requires close monitoring during initiation

paths.label: Option D
paths.survival: Not a standalone treatment — significantly improves regulation accuracy when combined with any insulin protocol
paths.aligns: Real-time glucose data replaces most spot-check glucose curves; dramatically reduces clinic visit frequency during dose adjustment phase
paths.tensions: Sensor placement on neck/flank requires practice; dogs may dislodge sensor; not all vets routinely support CGM data review; requires owner comfort with app-based monitoring

prognosis_bullets: Uncomplicated DM (no DKA, no concurrent illness): ~80% of dogs achieve stable glucose regulation within 1–3 months of insulin initiation
Median survival after diagnosis with good management: 2–3 years; many dogs with well-managed DM live 4–5+ years post-diagnosis
Cataracts develop in ~75% of diabetic dogs within 12 months — proactive discussion of preventive eye drops and surgical options is strongly advised
Concurrent conditions (hypothyroidism, Cushing's disease, UTI) frequently cause insulin resistance — screen every 6 months even when glucose appears controlled
Unlike cats, spontaneous insulin remission is rare in dogs — lifelong twice-daily insulin therapy is the realistic expectation
prognosis_note: Molly's presentation is encouraging: no ketoacidosis, stable vitals, and kidney function intact. Starting Vetsulin now with a consistent high-fiber diet gives her an excellent chance of long-term stable control. The cataract conversation is worth having with your vet now — by the time cataracts appear, the prevention window has passed.
